newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan troops find Tamil rebel coffin factory.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan troops find Tamil rebel coffin factory.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops hunting Tamil Tiger guerrillas in eastern jungle found a coffin factory when they raided an abandoned rebel base on Monday, a military spokesman said on Tuesday.

The troops found partly-made coffins and timber for their manufacture during the raid on the rebel complex in the jungle of Kokkaddicholai in Batticaloa district, 200 km (125 miles) east of the capital Colombo, he said.
Military officials said the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels were known to mass-produce coffins to carry their dead from battles with government forces.
The offensive on rebel jungle bases by four battalions, including commandos and special forces, was launched after the Tigers overran a police commando base in the area last Wednesday.

In a pre-dawn attack, the Tigers overran the camp at Pulukunava, killing 36 security personnel and two civilian helpers, and wounding 37. It was their biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
Rebel radio transmissions monitored by the army indicated 34 guerrillas died in the attack, the military said.
The Tigers captured a large haul of arms, including an 85 mm artillery piece and two mortars.
Troops who reached Kokkaddicholai town on Tuesday morning found only women and children, all the men having fled ahead of the advancing army, military officials said.
Another rebel jungle base in the area came under air and artillery attacks on Tuesday, they said, adding that there was no immediate word on guerrilla casualties.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the death toll is much higher.
